title: Adaptive retry budgets + streaming grace window: cross-SDK defaults and idempotency migration playbook
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create a pragmatic, cross-language playbook that standardizes: 1) default retry/backoff budgets for sync and streaming RPCs; 2) a streaming "grace window" (anchor) to reduce duplicate downstream processing; 3) a backwards-compatible idempotency key migration path and recommended id-key format; and 4) concrete Python/TS/Go examples + telemetry hooks. Aim: make SDK defaults safe for production mobile/web workloads while keeping ergonomics for PLG users.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Asha Raman: Initial ticket. Motivation: multiple customers observed cost spikes from aggressive client retries during transient infra blips; streaming reconnect storms also caused doubled output in backend processors. We need cross-SDK guardrails that are conservative by default and opt-in for aggressive modes.

2025-02-18 - Marco Diaz: Spike summary: bench runs across python/ts/go clients against a local runtime using a flaky network sim. Findings: naive 3x immediate retries increased request volume 2.7x and median tail latency; adding a small jittered exponential backoff recovered stability. Streaming reconnects without a grace window resulted in duplicated 'done' events in 6% of reconnect cases.

2025-02-20 - Design decision (proposal):
- Default sync retry policy: max_attempts=2 (1 retry), backoff: base=120ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=2000ms, jitter=0.2
- Retry budget: default token bucket with refill_rate=1/sec and burst=2 per-client (prevents client from amplifying during retries)
- Streaming grace window (anchor): 6s by default; on reconnect resume, server will treat events within anchor as potentially duplicate and provide resume token semantics
- Idempotency key format v1: "sdk-v1:{client_uuid}:{endpoint}:{fingerprint_sha1}"; recommend short-lived rotation and server-side dedupe window of 2 minutes
These defaults aim to balance latency and downstream cost; open to tuning after canary.

2025-02-24 - PM review (Lina Chen): Confirmed customer impact classification as medium. Request: provide sample opt-in aggressive profile for high-throughput internal services and a migration checklist for customers rolling id-key format changes.

2025-02-25 - Marco Diaz: Implementation plan:
1) Add shared retry module in each SDK with common semantics + platform-specific jitter RNG
2) Expose RetryPolicy object and high-level helper presets: SAFE_DEFAULT, HIGH_THROUGHPUT (opt-in)
3) Streaming client: implement reconnect backoff with 'anchor' semantics; include resume token exchange header X-RW-RESUME
4) Server: add dedupe window based on id-key and resume token; record telemetry metrics: retry_attempts, deduped_events, anchor_resumes

We should standardize metric tags: sdk_lang, retry_preset, endpoint, tenant_id (opt). Add sampling to low-level telemetry to avoid observability cost.

2025-03-03 - QA (Rajat Singh): Test matrix ready. Includes flaky network scenarios, high-concurrency replay, and id-key rotation tests. Edge cases: when id-key absent - server fallback policy should be 'stateless best-effort' and client should warn. Test plan references: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1___test_matrix

2025-03-04 - Asha Raman: Minor tweak to defaults after internal canary feedback: increase streaming anchor to 8s for mobile clients with poor connectivity; add opt-out flag for anchor in SDK constructor (enable_anchor: true). Also decided: migration path for id-key format will accept both v1 and v2 for 30 days, with a warning header when server receives a deprecated key.
